trim.summary: Trimming is not part of the current Cephalon support contract.

nativeAot.summary: Native AOT is not part of the current Cephalon support contract.

singleFile.summary: Single-file publishing is not part of the current Cephalon support contract.

representativePublishTargets.comment: List the smallest set of csproj paths the harness should publish to honestly prove a claim. The harness defaults to this list when -PublishTargets is not passed and -SkipPublish is not set; pass -SkipPublish to force audit-only mode. Each target is published once per deployment mode (trim / nativeAot / singleFile); the audit-only verdict reports warnings but does not fail the build because the manifest still declares all three modes as not-claimed.

deploymentModeEligibility.comment: Per-package eligibility table seeded from docs/trim-aot-hazard-inventory.md. Originally introduced via ENG-426 (high + first medium-tier seeding); broadened via ENG-432 (Cephalon.Behaviors.Http reclassified low->medium with three additional reflection sites), ENG-433 (Cephalon.Data added at medium tier under broadened MakeGenericMethod / BindingFlags pattern set), ENG-434 (Cephalon.Data.MySql added at high tier + Cephalon.Data.Postgres / Cephalon.Data.Oracle added at medium tier for the CDC capture services), ENG-435 (Cephalon.Abstractions added at low tier + two enum-extension hazard sites appended to Cephalon.Behaviors.Http), ENG-436 (six additional knownHazards entries appended to Cephalon.Behaviors covering the BehaviorModule.cs two-phase auto-registration pipeline + the BehaviorExecutionSlot.cs open-generic execution-slot dispatch — package tier unchanged at high, hazard list grows), ENG-437 (seven additional knownHazards entries appended to Cephalon.Behaviors.Http covering RestBehaviorProjection.cs reflective method lookup + open-generic dispatch, RestBehaviorModuleBuilder.cs IBehaviorModuleBuilder.Add overload selection + open-generic dispatch, and BehaviorRestProfileResolver.cs phase-1 ContainsBehaviorsAttribute.RegistrationType reflective enumerators — package tier unchanged at medium, hazard list grows from 6 to 13), ENG-438 (Cephalon.ReferenceDocs added at high tier with a permanent not-claimed posture — the published documentation generator performs by-design type-introspection of arbitrary referenced assemblies, so the high-tier remediation alternative "document a permanent not-claimed posture for that package" is the durable answer rather than a structural rewrite — closing the last item in the original ENG-433 not-yet-classified callout), and ENG-439 (Cephalon.ReferenceDocs csproj posture uplift — declared IsTrimmable=false / IsAotCompatible=false / PublishTrimmed=false / PublishAot=false / PublishSingleFile=false in src/Cephalon.ReferenceDocs/Cephalon.ReferenceDocs.csproj and seeded the matching requiredProjectProperties array in this manifest entry, so the harness's project-property audit phase can confirm the permanent posture in machine-checkable form). Each entry records the package's claim-audit tier, the actual reflection / dynamic-code call sites observed in its src/Cephalon.* source as of May 5, 2026, and the supportedModes a future claim could advertise (today: empty for every entry — the global manifest claim stays not-claimed until project properties + harness verdicts move). The list intentionally only enumerates packages that are NOT clean-baseline; the harness's project-property and analyzer audit phases scan all src/Cephalon.*.csproj automatically, so the absence of a package here means clean-baseline (no observed source-level hazard) rather than untracked. Excluded-by-design analyzer / source-generator projects are listed separately so the harness can confirm their disable-properties remain in place.

knownHazards.pattern: Activator.CreateInstance(moduleType, nonPublic: true)
knownHazards.remediation: Replace assembly-scanned module discovery with a compile-time module manifest emitted by a source generator that registers IModule descriptors at startup.

knownHazards.remediation: Annotation-recoverable in isolation via [DynamicallyAccessedMembers(PublicMethods | NonPublicMethods)] on ContainsBehaviorsAttribute.RegistrationType; package tier still gated by the phase-2 assembly-scan fallback below, so the structural fix is the same source-gen-emitted compile-time module manifest that retires BehaviorTypeRegistry.

knownHazards.pattern: regType.GetMethod("GetTopologyDescriptors", BindingFlags.Static | BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.NonPublic, null, Type.EmptyTypes, null) — phase-1 reflective lookup of the source-gen-emitted topology-descriptor enumerator (matching Invoke on line 360)
knownHazards.remediation: Same annotation-recovery + structural fix as the line-345 entry.

knownHazards.pattern: regType.GetMethod("GetBehaviorsNeedingRuntimeTopology", BindingFlags.Static | BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.NonPublic, null, Type.EmptyTypes, null) — phase-1 reflective lookup of the source-gen-emitted runtime-topology enumerator (matching Invoke on line 392)
knownHazards.remediation: Same annotation-recovery + structural fix as the line-345 entry.

knownHazards.pattern: assembly.DefinedTypes.Select(ti => ti.AsType()).ToArray() then Attribute.GetCustomAttribute(type, typeof(AppBehaviorAttribute)) plus type.GetInterfaces().FirstOrDefault(i => i.IsGenericType && i.GetGenericTypeDefinition() == typeof(IAppBehavior<,>)) — phase-2 reflection-fallback assembly scan over every type in the assembly
knownHazards.remediation: Source-gen-emitted compile-time module manifest that enumerates behaviors at build time, retiring both the assembly scan here and the BehaviorTypeRegistry runtime registry. Annotation alone is not sufficient — this is the dominant high-tier driver in the file.

knownHazards.pattern: behaviorType.GetMethod("ConfigureTopology", BindingFlags.Static | BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.FlattenHierarchy, null, [typeof(IBehaviorTopologyBuilder)], null) — reflective lookup of the optional static ConfigureTopology helper on each behavior type (matching Invoke on line 502)
knownHazards.remediation: Reachable from both phase-1 and phase-2; the phase-2 reach makes it high. Removed by the same source-gen-emitted module manifest that retires the assembly scan and BehaviorTypeRegistry.

knownHazards.pattern: typeof(BehaviorExecutionSlot).GetMethod(nameof(For), BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.Static)!.MakeGenericMethod(behaviorType, tIn, tOut) followed by forMethod.Invoke(null, null) (line 76) — open-generic method dispatch over the (behaviorType, TInput, TOutput) triple drawn from the runtime registry
knownHazards.remediation: Source-gen-emitted dispatch table keyed by behavior identity that materializes the closed generic For<TBehavior, TInput, TOutput>() at compile time. Same structural fix as the BehaviorTypeRegistry retirement above; high here (rather than medium like BehaviorRestEndpointGroup.cs:486) because behaviorType is sourced from the assembly-scanned registry rather than from a closed compile-time profile.

knownHazards.pattern: type.GetConstructors(BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.Instance | BindingFlags.Static | BindingFlags.DeclaredOnly) over an arbitrary runtime Type parameter — by-design enumeration of the public-and-static constructors of any type the generator is asked to document, used to emit per-constructor MemberPage entries
knownHazards.remediation: Permanent not-claimed posture for the package (the high-tier remediation alternative). The package's purpose is type-introspection of arbitrary referenced assemblies, so a source-generator-emitted descriptor table cannot replace this reflection without removing the package's reason to exist. A future slice may declare IsTrimmable=false; IsAotCompatible=false; PublishTrimmed=false; PublishAot=false; PublishSingleFile=false in the csproj to make the permanent posture machine-checkable through the harness's project-property audit phase.

knownTransitiveHazards.comment: Known third-party packages that emit trim or AOT warnings even when the consuming Cephalon.* project itself looks clean. Listed for reference; the harness does not currently fail on these but reports them in the per-target warnings list so the operator can see the source.
singleFile: Plugins or providers that load assemblies dynamically at runtime
